description: Deck intake v1.8.0 (FIX 30, Trevor ruling): 23 numbered conversational turns, down from 58 one-per-turn rows. Each turn row (kind 'merged') may return several legacy subfields; conditional subfields write documented defaults/derived values, never null. Alias rows ("alias": true) keep the exact legacy ids/prompts/enums for consumers that pin physical rows (interview-app payload, anti-fab checks, drift driver) and are filtered out of the ask sequence while PRESENTATION_INTAKE_V2 is on. PRESENTATION_INTAKE_V2=0 restores the legacy ask-all-rows behavior. Waiver and store-target contracts unchanged.

legacy_field_mapping._comment: Canonical mapping table (SOURCE OF TRUTH mirrored in deck-intake-driver.py:derive_legacy_fields). presentation_type -> {deck_type, creation_mode, presentation_mode, audience_mode}. Applied automatically the moment the driver records a validated presentation_type answer, and again at --complete when it writes/merges working/copy/intake.json.

signature.note: creation_mode defaults to from_scratch; overridden to content_personal/content_general by the signature_source follow-up when the client is converting existing material into the signature talk. Never left unset (AF-MODE-UNSET).

questions.prompt: What are we building: from scratch, from your content for one person, from your content for a broader audience, or a 4-phase Signature Presentation? If content-based, name/share the source and give the one core idea the audience must retain.

questions.prompt: Who is this for? Name the recipient if it is one person; otherwise describe the room (industry, situation, pain point, gender/cultural mix) and give the image-cast percentages you want, including 'no people' if applicable.
What specific book, program, message, framework, or named method is this deck grounded in? Give its name and a one-line description; say 'no named method' if there isn't one.
In one response: what is the presentation for, what exact action should people take at the end, and how should they feel when they leave?
Describe the honest before-and-after transformation, the #1 reason people may say no, and the real timeframe to see the result.
What line should they leave humming, if you have one, and what tone should carry it: inspirational, tough love, challenger, teacher, storyteller, high energy, calm premium, or a two-tone blend?

hook_seed.none_value: propose (never canonized as a client line)

questions.prompt: How long should the talk run, and do you have a hard slide-count target or should duration math decide?

slide_count.note: blank slide count derived from duration: max(1, round(duration_min * 0.8)) at ~1.25 slides/minute

questions.prompt: When must this be live, and is there anything else that could change the build?
Choose QUICK for essential defaults or IN-DEPTH for maximum control.

standard_mode.note: answer selects later optional detail; never changes the 23-turn ceiling

questions.prompt: I detected these presentation providers and plans: [redacted detected summary]. Confirm the plan/tier for any provider whose concurrency cannot be detected, or choose 'use conservative default.'

resource_plan.note: FIX 8: asked once when probe data is incomplete, then locked via resource_profile.is_plan_locked; never re-asked

questions.help: Ask-once contract (FIX 8): this is the ONLY question this interview ever asks about plans/limits. It is asked only when the automatic probe could not determine a provider's concurrency (capacity.probe()['resource_profile']['pending_questions'] is non-empty); a fully detected client is never asked it. The machine lock lives in resource_profile.py -- after the answer is recorded it is marked locked, copied into the capacity override, and NO later run or probe refresh ever re-asks. A decline ('use conservative default') is recorded the same way and keeps the conservative default (3). Never paste credentials, API keys, endpoints, or any account identifier anywhere in this answer -- plan tier name only.
questions.resolverHint: Feeds resource_profile.record_plan_answer/provider/plan -> capacity.persist_plan_answer() projects the locked ceiling into capacity_override.json, and scripts/presentation_job/resource_profile.py stores the locked profile (never in-repo, never printed verbatim -- redaction contract). ASK ONLY when capacity.probe()['resource_profile']['pending_intake_ids'] contains 'resource_plan'; after record_plan_answer (or record_conservative_default for the decline) it is locked and pending_questions() returns empty forever, which is the ask-once proof surface. Probe refresh (apply_probe_refresh) updates detected fields WITHOUT touching the lock.

questions.prompt: Name the offer this deck sells and lay out the stack (what the buyer actually gets, in their words).
Is there an event price, or is access free?

access_free.note: derived from event_price on the same turn, then confirmed

questions.prompt: Is the price a straight number or a drop (anchor then reveal)? Give the final price and the anchor if it drops.
Any payment plan? Any VIP tier (what it includes, its price, how many spots)?
What proof goes in: results, testimonials, screenshots, receipts? Paste or name the assets you want used.
Style: fresh clean-white default, or match brand? Give the primary brand color/logo source, any style preferences, and say if dark slides are OK.
How should visuals mix people, product, and text on slides? (Cast demographics follow your answer above.)
Where does the logo go? Blank means cover and closing slide only.
Core deliverables check: deck, teleprompter, speech script, audio deliverable. Say no to any you don't want (reasons are captured in one later turn).
Where should I deliver the finished deck, and do you want it uploaded into GoHighLevel?
Do you want the sales/checkout page and a VSL page built alongside the deck?
Want an audio demo of the talk? Pick a pace: default, medium, or fast (or give a words-per-minute target).

target_wpm.note: blank WPM derives: default=130, medium=140, fast=155

questions.prompt: For anything you said no to above (teleprompter, speech script, GHL upload, audio deliverable, sales/checkout, VSL page), give the reason in one sentence each, or say 'no note' per item.

What kind of presentation is this? (1) From scratch -- we brainstorm and build it new. (2) From your content -- personal: turn something you already have (deck/video/transcript) into a presentation for ONE specific person. (3) From your content -- general: turn existing content into a presentation for a room/mass audience. (4) Signature Presentation -- the 4-phase, 100+-slide signature talk (The Rulebook / The Vault / The Quest / The Original).
questions.help: This single answer decides everything downstream -- deck type, creation mode, presentation mode, and audience mode are all derived automatically from it (see legacy_field_mapping at the top of this file). You never have to answer those separately. There is no default: this question must be answered by the client -- an unanswered or unrecognized answer must never be treated as 'from_scratch' or any other type. [FIX 30 alias row: captured inside merged turn 1; kept for legacy consumers. Set PRESENTATION_INTAKE_V2=0 to ask this row directly.]

value_labels.from_scratch: From scratch -- brainstorm and build new
value_labels.content_personal: From your content -- personal (one specific recipient)

questions.resolverHint: No default: if the owner says 'no preference' or does not answer, do NOT guess -- re-ask, or escalate to the operator. Landmine closed (2026-08-18): this question used to carry a JSON `default: from_scratch` that a required:false flip (or any consumer treating absence as approval) could silently re-arm, producing a webinar for every client who never actually answered. An absent or unrecognized presentation_type answer must fail closed -- see UngroundedDeckTypeError in intake_writer.py and _normalize_enum_value in deck-intake-driver.py, both of which now refuse to fabricate a value here. The driver derives deck_type, creation_mode, presentation_mode, and audience_mode from this ONE answer via derive_legacy_fields() (deck-intake-driver.py) the moment it is validated -- never ask those four as separate questions. 'content_personal' additionally requires recipient_name (asked immediately after, order 0.3) and extracted_substance before build (per _chk_mode); 'content_general' requires extracted_substance. 'signature': the driver asks ONE conditional follow-up ('signature_source', order 0.5: is this built from existing content?), sets deck_type:signature_presentation in working/copy/intake.json, and routes to the Signature Presentation Architect / brainstorming-buddy-presentations SIGNATURE mode, which is choice-first (QUICK vs IN-DEPTH) and then asks the SACRED 8 Questions + the frame-selection question ONE at a time -- never a batch (dumping them is AF-INTAKE-BATCH) -- assembling the answers into ONE atomic record per 51-signature-presentation/intake/sp-8-questions.json (deck-intake-driver.py signature mode). The frame is captured THERE as signature_frame (rulebook|vault|quest|original), not here. Director Mode A/B is NEVER asked -- it stays derived from whether source assets exist (director-of-presentations.md SOP 9.3). This question runs BEFORE the standard one-question-per-turn capture below; every question below behaves exactly as today regardless of presentation_type.

This is the SUBSTANCE the deck is extracted FROM -- build_deck.py's AF-MODE-UNSET gate refuses a content-mode deck that has none (SOP-MODE-00, P22-P29). It is the client's own words, never the assistant's summary. [FIX 30 alias row: captured inside merged turn 1; kept for legacy consumers. Set PRESENTATION_INTAKE_V2=0 to ask this row directly.]
questions.resolverHint: Ask ONLY when presentation_type is content_personal or content_general; auto-skipped for from_scratch and signature. The validated answer is lifted verbatim into working/copy/intake.json.extracted_substance by _apply_type_picker_derivation -- never paraphrased, never defaulted. There is no default: an empty answer must be re-asked.

questions.resolverHint: Ask only when presentation_type=='signature'. Default if unanswered: from_scratch. questions.prompt: Do you need me to create a sales page and a checkout page to go along with your presentation? (yes / no)

A 'no' is recorded as a CLIENT WAIVER with the client's own words -- it is never inferred from silence and never written by the assistant. A 'no' gates OUT the sales+checkout branch entirely. [FIX 30 alias row: captured inside merged turn 21; kept for legacy consumers. Set PRESENTATION_INTAKE_V2=0 to ask this row directly.]

questions.resolverHint: Default 'yes' when the owner says 'whatever you recommend' or does not answer. Only an explicit 'no' opens the follow-up. Never mark 'no' on the client's behalf; never summarise their reason -- the follow-up answer is stored VERBATIM as the waiver's client_request_quote. A 'no' gates OUT the sales+checkout branch (deck-only or VSL-only run); a 'yes' enables the P-U-SALES-* / P-U-CHECKOUT-* / P-U-FORM-CHECKOUT phases.

waiver_field_mapping._comment: U026 — the CONSENT record. Each entry maps a gate key (see the engine's Gates class) to the intake question that captures the client's own decision, plus the conditional follow-up that captures their VERBATIM words when they decline. A gate may be waived ONLY by a record carrying a non-empty client_request_quote. Silence is NOT consent: every toggle here is required+block_gate, so --complete cannot pass while one is unanswered. prompt_floor and qc are deliberately ABSENT — a client cannot consent to a thinner prompt or a lower quality bar; those are craft floors, not options.
